sources.title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
sources.authors: Amey Agrawal, Nitin Kedia, Ashish Panwar, Jayashree Mohan, Nipun Kwatra, Bhargav S. Gulavani, Alexey Tumanov, Ramachandran Ramjee
sources.readset: Full paper, references and artifact appendix read; case claims checked against sections 4.1-4.3, section 5 setup, Figure 9, Figure 14, Table 4 and section 6. Key physical PDF pages 8, 9, 10, 11, 13 and 14 visually inspected during grounding; curves were not digitized.
sources.rights_note: Publisher open access establishes readability, not a blanket redistribution or adaptation license. Only an original attributed explanation is packaged; raw PDF, extracted text, images, figures and supplier synthesis are excluded.

applicability: Source-supported hypothesis selection when observed long prefills interfere with ongoing decodes
Chunked-prefill token-budget tradeoffs under specified latency, workload, hardware and parallelism conditions

findings.direction: Split a long prefill into chunks and combine them with ongoing decodes
findings.reason: Source mechanism for long prefills interrupting token generation; chunking limits prefill work per iteration but does not make that work free. Figure 9 still shows added batch latency relative to decode-only execution
findings.revisit_when: Diagnose queueing, memory shortage or suspended requests first; only attribute the delay to prefill interference after that

findings.direction: Tighten the token budget with smaller chunks
findings.reason: Smaller chunks reduce prefill work per iteration but can lower compute utilization and repeat fixed launch costs
findings.revisit_when: Profile the actual utilization and launch overhead for the target hardware before choosing a budget

findings.direction: Accept the KV re-read cost of later chunks
findings.reason: Each later chunk attends to earlier chunks of the same prompt, rereading their KV cache. The source distinguishes these additional memory reads from unchanged attention computation
findings.revisit_when: Account for the extra memory reads separately from attention compute when estimating cost

findings.direction: Pick a budget without accounting for tile boundaries or pipeline parallelism
findings.reason: Matrix tile boundaries affect execution cost and neighboring token counts need not have neighboring runtimes; with pipeline parallelism, batch runtime differences can leave stages idle
findings.revisit_when: Measure runtime across neighboring token counts and check stage idling before fixing a budget

findings.direction: Read Table 4 as an all-round improvement
findings.reason: The combined design has lower P99 TBT than either component alone, but its P50 TTFT is higher than hybrid-batching-only. It trades first-token latency against tighter token gaps
findings.revisit_when: State which metric the deployment optimizes; the combined design does not improve every metric over each alternative

limitations: Paper-author observations and proposed adaptation checks are not local measurements or current-engine support.
The combined design does not beat hybrid-only P50 TTFT in either Table 4 trace.
No universal budget, fairness guarantee, quantitative disaggregation comparison or empirical skill efficacy is established.
Raw source redistribution and adaptation permission remain UNKNOWN.
